function.description: This function is used to create a recommendation model using a given user data and an algorithm type Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_data.description: A data frame of user ratings. Rows represent users, columns represent items, and entries represent user ratings for items

algorithm.description: The algorithm to be used for creating the recommendation model. Collaborative filtering, content-based filtering and hybrid filtering.

matrix_factorization.description: Optional parameter to indicate whether matrix factorization should be used. Default is False.

Below is a practical, step‑by‑step guide you can follow (or adapt) to build a modern, production‑ready frontend for your e‑commerce site. I’ll cover the whole pipeline – from choosing a stack to deploying – and sprinkle in code snippets, best‑practice tips, and links to useful resources. --- ## 1️⃣ Pick Your Tech Stack | Goal | Recommended Framework | Why | |------|-----------------------|-----| | **Fast, component‑driven UI** | **React** (Create‑React‑App / Vite) | Huge ecosystem, great tooling, mature community. | | **Opinionated, batteries‑included** | **Vue 3** (Vite + Pinia) | Simpler learning curve, excellent docs. | | **Enterprise‑grade, full‑stack** | **Angular** | Built‑in DI, RxJS, CLI, TypeScript everywhere. | | **Static‑site generator** | **Next.js** (React) | Server‑side rendering, image optimisation, API routes. | | **Mobile‑first SPA** | **SvelteKit** | Tiny bundle size, reactive compiler. | > **Tip:** If you already have a backend in Node/Express, Next.js gives you a single repo for both API routes and pages. If you’re using a headless CMS or GraphQL, consider Apollo Client + React or Urql + SvelteKit. --- ## 2️⃣ Project Skeleton & Tooling ```bash # Example with Vite + React + TypeScript npm create vite@latest ecommerce-frontend -- --template react-ts cd ecommerce-frontend npm install ``` ### Core Dependencies | Purpose | Package | Notes | |---------|---------|-------| | State mgmt | **Redux Toolkit** (React) / **Pinia** (Vue) / **NgRx** (Angular) | Use RTK Query for auto‑generated hooks. | | Routing | **React Router v6** / **Vue Router** / **Angular Router** | Keep nested routes for product categories. | | Styling | **Tailwind CSS** (utility‑first) | Or **styled-components** if you prefer CSS‑in‑JS. | | Forms | **react-hook-form** / **vee‑validate** | Handles validation declaratively. | | HTTP client | **Axios** / **fetch** | Wrap in a service layer. | | Testing | **Jest** + **React Testing Library** | Snapshot tests + unit tests. | | Linting | **ESLint** + **Prettier** | Enforce style consistency. | | CI/CD | GitHub Actions / GitLab CI | Automate lint, test, build, deploy. | --- ## 3️⃣ Design & Wireframing 1. **Sketch the core pages** - Home / Landing - Category listing - Product detail - Cart / Checkout flow - User account (login, profile, orders) 2. **Use Figma / Sketch** to create high‑fidelity mockups. - Export assets as SVGs or use icon libraries like **Heroicons** or **Font Awesome**. 3. **Accessibility audit** - Ensure color contrast, semantic HTML, ARIA labels. - Run axe-core or Lighthouse. --- ## 4️⃣ Build the Component Hierarchy ```text src/ ├─ components/ │ ├─ Header.tsx │ ├─ Footer.tsx │ ├─ ProductCard.tsx │ ├─ CartIcon.tsx │ └─ ... ├─ pages/ │ ├─ HomePage.tsx │ ├─ CategoryPage.tsx │ ├─ ProductPage.tsx │ ├─ CartPage.tsx │ └─ CheckoutPage.tsx ├─ services/ │ └─ api.ts # Axios instance + typed endpoints ├─ store/ │ ├─ cartSlice.ts │ ├─ productsSlice.ts │ └─ authSlice.ts └─ App.tsx ``` ### Example: `api.ts` (Axios wrapper) ```ts import axios from 'axios'; const api = axios.create({ baseURL: import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL, timeout: 10000, }); export const fetchProducts = async () => { const { data } = await api.get('/products'); return data; }; export const addToCart = async (productId: number, qty: number) => { const { data } = await api.post('/cart', { productId, qty }); return data; }; ``` --- ## 5️⃣ State Management & Data Flow ### Using Redux Toolkit + RTK Query (React) ```ts // src/store/productsSlice.ts import { createApi, fetchBaseQuery } from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react'; export const productsApi = createApi({ reducerPath: 'productsApi', baseQuery: fetchBaseQuery({ baseUrl: '/api' }), endpoints: (builder) => ({ getAllProducts: builder.query({ query: () => '/products', }), getProductById: builder.query({ query: (id) => `/products/${id}`, }), }), }); export const { useGetAllProductsQuery, useGetProductByIdQuery } = productsApi; ``` ### Using Pinia (Vue) ```ts // src/stores/cartStore.ts import { defineStore } from 'pinia'; import { api } from '@/services/api'; export const useCartStore = defineStore('cart', { state: () => ({ items: [] as CartItem[], }), actions: { async loadCart() { this.items = await api.get('/cart').then(r => r.data); }, async addItem(productId: number, qty: number) { await api.post('/cart', { productId, qty }); await this.loadCart(); }, }, }); ``` --- ## 6️⃣ Routing & Navigation ```tsx // src/App.tsx (React Router v6) import { BrowserRouter, Routes, Route } from 'react-router-dom'; import HomePage from './pages/HomePage'; import CategoryPage from './pages/CategoryPage'; import ProductPage from './pages/ProductPage'; import CartPage from './pages/CartPage'; import CheckoutPage from './pages/CheckoutPage'; function App() { return (
} /> } /> } /> } /> } />
); } ``` --- ## 7️⃣ Styling & Responsiveness ### Tailwind CSS Setup ```bash npm i -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer npx tailwindcss init -p ``` Add to `tailwind.config.js`: ```js module.exports = { content: ['./index.html', './src/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}'], theme: { extend: {}, }, plugins: [], }; ``` Example component: ```tsx // src/components/ProductCard.tsx export default function ProductCard({ product }) { return (

{product.name}

${product.price.toFixed(2)}

); } ``` --- ## 8️⃣ Performance Optimisation | Technique | How | |-----------|-----| | Code splitting | `React.lazy()` + `Suspense` or dynamic imports in Vue. | | Image optimisation | Use `` component (Next.js) or `loading="lazy"` + `srcset`. | | Prefetch critical data | `prefetchQuery` in RTK Query or `prefetch` in Vue Query. | | Bundle analysis | `webpack-bundle-analyzer` or `vite-plugin-inspect`. | | Service worker | Workbox or Vite’s PWA plugin for offline caching. | --- ## 9️⃣ Testing Strategy | Layer | Tool | Focus | |-------|------|-------| | Unit | Jest + React Testing Library | Component logic, hooks. | | Integration | Cypress | End‑to‑end flows (add to cart, checkout). | | Visual | Storybook | Isolated component view + accessibility addon. | Example unit test: ```tsx // src/pages/__tests__/ProductPage.test.tsx import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react'; import { Provider } from 'react-redux'; import { store } from '@/store'; import ProductPage from '../ProductPage'; import { MemoryRouter, Route, Routes } from 'react-router-dom'; test('renders product details', async () => { render( } /> ); expect(await screen.findByText(/Loading/i)).not.toBeInTheDocument(); expect(screen.getByRole('heading')).toHaveTextContent(/Product Name/i); }); ``` --- ## 🔟 Deployment & DevOps | Platform | Steps | |----------|-------| | Netlify | Connect repo → Build command `npm run build` → Publish directory `dist`. Enable SSR via Netlify Functions if needed. | | Vercel | Similar to Netlify; great for Next.js. | | Render | Deploy static site or Docker container. | | Docker | `docker build -t my-ecommerce .` + push to registry. | | CI | GitHub Actions: lint → test → build → deploy. Example workflow:** ```yaml name: CI/CD on: push: branches: [main] pull_request: jobs: build-test: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: '20' - run: npm ci - run: npm run lint - run: npm run test - run: npm run build - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4 with: name: build path: dist deploy: needs: build-test runs-on: ubuntu-latest environment: production steps: - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4 with: name: build - uses: peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v3 with: github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} publish_dir: ./dist ``` --- ## 📚 Resources & Further Reading | Topic | Link | |-------|------| | React Docs | https://react.dev | | Vue 3 Docs | https://vuejs.org | | Angular Docs | https://angular.io | | Tailwind CSS | https://tailwindcss.com | | RTK Query | https://redux-toolkit.js.org/api/createApi | | Pinia | https://pinia.vuejs.org | | Accessibility Checklist | https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.0 | | Lighthouse Audits | https://developers.google.com/web/tools/lighthouse | | Vite Docs | https://vitejs.dev | | Next.js Docs | https://nextjs.org/docs | --- ### Quick Checklist Before You Hit “Deploy” 1. ✅ All critical paths (home → product → cart → checkout) work end‑to‑end. 2. ✅ Responsive layout passes mobile viewport tests. 3. ✅ Lighthouse score ≥ 90 (performance, accessibility, best practices). 4. ✅ Unit tests ≥ 80% coverage. 5. ✅ CI pipeline builds without errors. --- #### Need help with a specific part? - Want a sample `Cart` component with RTK Query? - Need guidance on setting up Stripe integration? - Curious how to add server‑side rendering for SEO? Just let me know which piece you’d like to dive deeper into!
